scope: Final revision 6 delta: expanded pre-Execute effect barrier addressing ASTRA2-R5-01; prior native provenance, full backup and conservative-name requirements retained.

findings.assessment: Whole PREPARE and EXECUTE requests each require exact grammar admission. Sole top-level classification, rejection of nested/multiple forms, immutable portal capture, shared connection-local namespace, and restrictions inside bodies/arguments preserve the intended all-client SQL boundary. Admission does not establish backend preparation success.

Read ASTRA2-R5-01 and revision 6. Revision 5 Q/E-only accounting omitted planning-time Bind effects and related hooks. Revision 6 conservatively marks Q/P/B/D/E/C/S before forwarding, so a later Q/P cannot overtake pending analysis, type input, planning/revalidation, cleanup or transaction completion effects. This resolves the cited design blocker without claiming function-effect analysis.

Native ASCII names are limited to 63 bytes and folded only for lookup. Conservatively reject protocol prepared statement names over 63 bytes in implementation: SQL EXECUTE truncation could otherwise select a backend object under an alias not represented by exact protocol-name lookup. This rejection is permitted by the specification conservative policy; do not normalize forwarded protocol strings.

Read current sql_guard.py and sql_proxy.py. They still reject PrepareStmt/ExecuteStmt and have no pending-effect Q/P lexical barrier. Their present behavior is baseline evidence, not revision 5 compliance. No production source was changed by this review.

Keep the complete native pg_dump/pg_restore path with ACLs and original revision 3 backup failure evidence. No ACL omission or backup-content reduction may be substituted for native preparation support. Unresolved upstream LICENSE/NOTICE provenance remains recorded; local authorized use does not grant redistribution or commercial license clearance.

Q/Sync enqueue their current cycle and then advance it. Matching Ready releases only effects at or before that barrier after validated lexical statuses; initial startup Ready is the sole unqueued exception. B/E/C/D/S/H and COPY continue while new source is blocked. COPY data/end remain attributed to the initiating Q/E, preventing orphan next-cycle pending effects. Malformed/unsolicited Ready closes the session; ignored frontend traffic cannot synthesize acknowledgements.

formal_review.assessment: The unchanged generic forwardEffect/completeCycle model supports every correctly marked effect, including newly specified pre-Execute messages. Its 28 policy lemmas do not prove message-effect classification, cycle assignment, queue correspondence or backend hooks. Revision 6 explicitly makes these adapter checks, rather than attributing their verification to Lean.
formal_review.adapter_trust: NativePrepare.bodyPart proves nonempty substring decomposition only. Correct top-level grammar classification, body/name extraction, PostgreSQL ASCII name correspondence, ordered unique cycle assignment and association of ReadyForQuery with its Q/Sync barrier remain adapter obligations.
formal_review.proof_execution: This review does not replace the required two clean Lean builds or assert their completion.

implementation_acceptance_obligations: Real unchanged full pg_dump and pg_restore including ACLs through canonical proxy endpoints; per-entry-point counter deltas and endpoint evidence, plus recovery and revocation integrity.

Native and both cross-protocol preparation paths; fresh-connection cached EXECUTE denial; unknown/cross-connection names; duplicate/failed native or protocol preparations; immutable old portals and state budgets.
Quoted/Unicode/overlong SQL names and over-63-byte protocol names reject conservatively; mixed-case native ASCII lookup does not rewrite SQL.
Opaque/nested/multiple statement forms and unsafe set_config/lexical expressions inside native PREPARE/EXECUTE reject before forwarding.

Delayed and fragmented backend status, E then P before Sync, Q then Q/P, older Ready after newer Execute, and an isolated pg_settings mutation cannot forward newly parsed SQL under stale mode assumptions.
Barrier progress with Sync/Flush/COPY/cancellation; successful matching safe completion permits later SQL on a session that has not been rejected. A rejected session stays closed.
Retain existing parser tamper/unavailable, exact bytes, framing, migration partial-recovery, database/RLS, ML-integrity and HTTP checks.
P followed by P before Sync rejects the second source; delayed Bind or Describe followed by Q/P also rejects before forwarding. Exercise ordinary P/B/D/E/S completion independently.

Exercise Close and Sync completion effects, multiple pending cycles with an older Ready after a newer marked message, unexpected Ready rejection, and COPY completion without orphan pending state. Audit runtime effect classification against pinned PostgreSQL source.
final_conclusion: Approve the exact revision 6 contract for implementation. Prior revision 5 approval was incomplete on pre-Execute effects; ASTRA2-R5-01 is now explicitly addressed. No runtime source changes or runtime/proof gate completion are asserted.
